surfaces.part: packed earth ground field with grain, clods and gravel flakes

answer.evidence: This is a seamless terrain tile: a flat, uniform ground texture spanning the full 192x144 image. The column scans show only irregular grain runs of L about 100-111, with scattered darker (#4a3828, #654c39) and lighter (#916f57) speckles and clods. There is no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse, roof or vertical face, and the silhouette is a constant 192 px wide for all rows. It reads as a flat ground surface with no standing object, so there is no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a ground patch of the same kind as the grass reference. It shows 4 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving. Near-flat coverage is 3%, so there are no large flat areas, and the fine 1px grain is visible across the field. There are no outlines to judge. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so any edge is tinted. The clods are small, soft, darker patches with little highlight/shadow shading, and the gravel and rust flakes are sparse single pixels. The raw palette is only 11 colours and 4 per tile, so each tile reads as one grain ramp. That is thinner than the grass reference, which has tufts, clumps and a darker patch, and much thinner than the paving, which has individually shaded stones. Texture is present but uniform. Raised clods lack the multi-step highlight and shadow shading (5-6 steps) that Beodeul uses, so the piece is competent but a bit shallow.
